**Title:** Which Dollar? Exchange Dollars as Exchange Rates in Web Crypto Prices

**Abstract (299 words):**

Crypto prices on the web are quoted in dollars, but an exchange's ledger dollar is a claim on that exchange and can trade away from a redeemable U.S. dollar. Prior work attributes cross-exchange bitcoin premia to such frictions without separating them from asset-specific movements. We develop an hourly decomposition that does. A shift in an exchange's dollar moves every asset there equally, so agreement across unrelated assets identifies the exchange's dollar exchange rate, and triangular parity checks it. Applied to Bitfinex, Coinbase and Bitstamp from 2017 to 2023, the decomposition showed that Bitfinex's dollar carried its own exchange rate throughout, with daily bitcoin and ether gaps against Bitstamp correlated at 0.949 or more in every year, while median bitcoin gaps between Coinbase and Bitstamp after 2018 were at most 2.3 basis points (bps) and mostly asset-specific. A single rate per exchange-hour, estimated from other assets, removed 85% of the mean-square cross-exchange gap for five assets withheld from development (99% in 2019, 30% to 45% in each later year), and made no correction for an exchange pair that shared a dollar. On Bitfinex, a monitor built on the decomposition, with a rule fixed in advance, raised 0.4 false alarm episodes per year, a third the rate of a plain price-gap alarm at equal recall, and flagged the exchange from October 2018, 6.5 months before regulators disclosed its loss. In 2023 it separated three shocks. Binance.US's dollar stood a median 557 bps from the U.S. dollar for 530 hours after its banks withdrew. The loss of Silvergate and Signature banking raised no alarm on any monitored exchange. The USDC run moved the token, not an exchange dollar, and Chainlink's bitcoin and ether feeds did not inherit the token's depeg. Aggregators and oracles can thus state which dollar a price is in.

**Suggested keywords:** exchange dollars; unit of account; truth discovery; price feeds and oracles; Web data quality; cryptocurrency markets; reproducibility
